newsitem.title: ZAIRE: ZAIRE REBELS PLAN TO RENEGOTIATE MINING CONTRACTS.
newsitem.headline: ZAIRE REBELS PLAN TO RENEGOTIATE MINING CONTRACTS.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's rebel forces, who now control over half Zaire, plan to renegotiate contracts with international mining companies, including De Beers Consolidated Mines, an official said on Monday.

In the short-term, foreign companies would be allowed to continue working under existing terms. But Kabila's financial commissioner (finance minister) Mwana Nanga Mawampanga told reporters these arrangements would soon be overhauled and put on a more equitable basis.
"In the short-run, we are telling them that they can continue to work in the framework of the present arrangements. A bad contract is after all better than no contract at all," he said.

"But at some point we are going to look at the fine print and make sure that we improve contracts where they can be improved...In other words we want to renegotiate in good faith to improve these contracts wherever possible."
Mawampanga said he was not happy with De Beers' monopoly position in the diamond industry.
"It is a monopoly and we don't want monopolies in this country anymore," he told a news conference.
"If they don't want to accept that, they will have to make up their own minds what to do. We will not tolerate monopolistic behaviour in this country."
De Beers announced earlier this month that its representatives had met with Kabila. It said at the time that discussions had focused on the security of its staff and facilities.
De Beers has buying offices in the rebel-held towns of Kisangani and Mbuji-Mayi and a contract to buy the production of the Miba mine at Mbuji-Mayi.
Miba is 80 percent owned by the Zaire government with Sibeka of Belgium owning the remaining 20 percent. De Beers holds 20 percent of Sibeka and so has a minor indirect stake in the Miba mine.
